input: It is important to note that gravity settlers play a crucial role in the removal of sand from process streams, and this passage delves into the key design considerations. The design is based on the overflow rate, which can be defined as the volumetric throughput divided by the plan area of the settler. With a throughput of 284 m3 h-1 and a design overflow rate of 0.53 m h-1, the required plan area works out to 536 m2. This parameter is particularly significant because, in an ideal settler, a particle is removed when its settling velocity exceeds the upward velocity of the liquid, and the overflow rate represents that upward velocity over the whole plan area, providing a convenient basis for sizing. The units themselves underscore the comparison: a throughput in m3 h-1 divided by an area in m2 returns a velocity in m h-1, the same unit as a settling velocity. It is worth noting that the design figure of 0.53 m h-1 is a vendor rule for sand, and the rule is specific to this solid; a finer or lighter solid would typically take a lower rate. Importantly, this figure was not measured on the stream to be treated, and no settling test on the actual slurry has been run, so the sizing stands on the vendor basis and carries the limitations associated with that basis. Factors such as particle size distribution, solids concentration and inlet distribution can each influence the removal achieved in practice, and the vendor figure does not account for any of them. The plan area of 536 m2 is the area required by the rule at the stated throughput; the length and width are not fixed by the sizing and will follow from the available plot and the inlet arrangement. Overall, a settling test on the actual slurry is the measurement that would replace the vendor rule with a site-specific value, and the area should be regarded as provisional until such a test has been carried out.
